info.title: FluentCRM API
info.description: Complete REST API documentation for FluentCRM — a self-hosted email marketing and CRM plugin for WordPress.

get.description:
Report everything the Settings → MCP screen needs to decide what to render: whether an adapter is installed and active, which one is providing it, how many abilities are registered, and whether the kill-switch is on.

An adapter can come from two places — the standalone adapter plugin or a bundled adapter inside FluentHub — and `adapter_provider` tells you which one won (`plugin`, `toolkit`, or an empty string when neither is active).

`tools_count` is 0 whenever the WordPress Abilities API is missing, since there is nowhere to register abilities.

<!-- fc:access -->

**Required capability:** `fcrm_manage_settings`

_Enforced by `SettingsPolicy::verifyRequest()`, the policy default for this route group._

<!-- /fc:access -->

adapter_installed.description: True when either the standalone adapter or FluentHub is present on disk.

adapter_active.description: True when an adapter runtime is actually available to serve MCP requests.

adapter_provider.description: Which source is providing the active adapter.

standalone_adapter_installed.description: True when the standalone adapter plugin is present.

toolkit_adapter_available.description: True when the loaded FluentHub build bundles an MCP adapter.

adapter_runtime_available.description: True when the adapter runtime classes are loadable.

adapter_version.description: Detected standalone adapter version, if any.

endpoint_url.description: Full URL of the MCP JSON-RPC endpoint.

tools_count.description: Number of registered FluentCRM abilities. 0 when the Abilities API is absent.

mcp_enabled.description: The kill-switch. Defaults to true; toggled by `POST /mcp/toggle`.

pro_active.description: True when FluentCampaign Pro is active, which adds further abilities.

app_passwords_url.description: Admin URL of the Application Passwords section.

plugins_url.description: Admin URL of the Plugins screen.

can_auto_install_adapter.description: True when a handler opted into background installation via the `fluent_toolkit/can_auto_install` filter.

current_user_login.description: Login of the requesting user, pre-filled into the generated snippets.

is_local_dev.description: Heuristic local-development detection — a dev TLD, `localhost`, or a private/loopback IP. Filterable via `fluent_crm/mcp_is_local_dev`.

401.description: Not authenticated — missing or invalid credentials.

403.description: Authenticated but the user lacks the capability this route requires.

ApplicationPasswords.name: Authorization
ApplicationPasswords.description: WordPress Application Passwords — use Basic auth with your WordPress username and an application password in the format: username:application_password
